header: Linking your object file with our test main
notes: observed: re/original-grade-txt/16_subseq.grade.txt has exactly two build lines, 'Attempting to compile maxSeq.c ' (trailing space) and 'Linking your object file with our test main' (recorded here as compileMessage and header), then the '#####...' separators with 'array size:0/1/100/5000 was Correct' as testcase2..5, and 'Overall Grade: A' (recorded as successVerdict). There is no testcase1: maxSeq.c defines no main, so the original's 'run your own main' step was skipped and the remaining cases kept their inherited numbering -- this config therefore sets no selfTest. 16_subseq/README gives the contract size_t maxSeq(int * array, size_t n) with the one-element series defined to have length 1. inferred: drivers/16_subseq/maxSeq_test.c -- no teacher object survives (re/elf/16_subseq__maxSeq.o.{md,json} is the student's own maxSeq.c compiled by the course Makefile: defined symbol maxSeq, imported puts; 16_subseq/ holds no other object), so the driver is reasoned from the artifacts above; the array contents (small values, so runs are short and repeats are common), the seed and the wrong-answer wording ('Incorrect') are inferred, while 'array size:%d was Correct' is observed. The reference answers for the four seeded arrays are 0, 1, 4 and 6, re-derived independently in Python while validating the driver; it catches the classic wrong answer (the *discontiguous* longest increasing subsequence) and an implementation that always returns 1. build.sources is empty and the driver #includes maxSeq.c with main renamed, so a main() a student may have left there for their own testing cannot collide; build.flags are deliberately lax because 16_subseq/Makefile compiles with no flags at all. Difference from the original: because there is no testcase1 to skip, the four driver cases are numbered 1..4 where the original's inherited numbering was 2..5 (its testcase1 was skipped because maxSeq.c has no main); every observed line is still reproduced.
